targetTexts.1: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him:
targetTexts.2: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
targetTexts.3: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.
targetTexts.4: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink,
targetTexts.5: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.
targetTexts.6: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.
targetTexts.7: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
targetTexts.8: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.
targetTexts.9: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
targetTexts.10: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
targetTexts.11: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
targetTexts.12: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.
targetTexts.13: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
targetTexts.14: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
targetTexts.15: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.
targetTexts.16: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
targetTexts.17: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
targetTexts.18: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
targetTexts.19: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
targetTexts.20: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
targetTexts.21: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
targetTexts.22: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
targetTexts.23: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land.
targetTexts.24: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
targetTexts.25: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
targetTexts.26: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
targetTexts.27: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
targetTexts.28: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:
targetTexts.29: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
targetTexts.30: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
targetTexts.31: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
